newsitem.title: USA: US oil demand up 1.1 percent first-half '97 - API.
newsitem.headline: US oil demand up 1.1 percent first-half '97 - API.

text.p: U.S. demand for petroleum rose 1.1 percent in the first half of 1997 from 1996, and averaged 18.39 million barrels per day, the American Petroleum Institute said Wednesday.
In its six-month summary, the API also said U.S. imports of crude oil and petroleum products jumped 5.5 percent from first-half 1996 and averaged 9.90 million barrels per day.

"Both domestically and internationally, supplies are increasing at a rate that has put downward pressure on prices. In the United States, the increased consumption is being driven by rapid economic growth and is concentrated in those areas that are most directly tied to the state of the economy," Edward Murphy, API analyst, said in a statement.
U.S. crude oil production dropped 1.4 percent in the first half of 1997 from a year ago, and averaged 6.4 million bpd, as Alaska production continued to drop.
Demand for gasoline rose 1.2 percent to 7.87 million barrels per day from 7.78 million in first-half last year, with a fairly modest rise in disposable personal income limiting gains.

Demand for distillates rose 1.8 percent from first-half 1996 to average 3.49 million bpd on strong economic growth, although gains were trimmed by unusually warm weather the first three months of 1997.
Demand for kerosene jet fuel rose 0.8 percent from first-half 1996 to average 1.57 million bpd, with strong underlying growth in aviation fuel use.
Residual fuel demand fell 3.8 percent from first-half 1997 to average 841,000 bpd.
Demand for other oils rose 1.9 percent in the first half of the year to average 4.65 million bpd, with growth largely due to petrochemical demand.
Input to crude distillation units rose 1.3 percent from first-half 1996, the API said.
